item.title: Trump to meet Venezuela acting president, first meeting since Maduro’s removal
item.description: President Donald Trump will meet acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodriguez in New York. This meeting occurs during a reception for leaders attending the UN General Assembly. The leaders are expected to discuss Venezuela's energy sector and a recent oil reserves agreement. This engagement follows Washington's removal of former President Nicolas Maduro in January. Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado faces uncertainty regarding her return to the country.

item.title: US reaches deal with Denmark for ‘permanent security control’ over Greenland, says Donald Trump
item.description: The United States has secured permanent security control over Greenland. This agreement allows Washington to act on the Arctic island for security needs. It prevents adversaries from establishing military bases or making sensitive investments. Denmark and Greenland expect to sign the deal soon. The agreement strengthens common security in the Arctic region.

item.title: In 2004, Ken Griffey Jr. paid $2.575 million for 11.58 lakefront acres near Orlando
item.description: Baseball legend Ken Griffey Jr. has placed his stunning lakeside mansion on the market for $27 million. Acquired in 2004, he dedicated four years to crafting this Mediterranean-style masterpiece, featuring seven luxurious bedrooms and ten bathrooms. The estate boasts exceptional amenities, including a private movie theater and a fun-filled saltwater pool complete with a waterslide. With his children now grown, Griffey is ready to pass on this remarkable home.

item.title: Trump bars news outlets CNN, MS NOW, Politico from White House
item.description: President Donald Trump has enacted a swift exclusion of three major news outlets—CNN, MS NOW, and Politico—from White House premises. He branded their regular reports as 'FAKE NEWS,' marking a bold stance against media he perceives as adversarial. Trump warned that more outlets could follow if they continue to publish misleading narratives about his presidency.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Rod Stewart’s former LA mansion & expanded 6-acre estate sold in two deals totaling $86M
item.description: A legendary estate in Holmby Hills, previously owned by Rod Stewart, has fetched an impressive $86 million. The sprawling six-acre property was split into two parcels, with television producer David Zander acquiring the main mansion for $57 million. Meanwhile, Nick Kaiser purchased a smaller parcel complete with a historic cabin for $29 million. This notable sale underscores the ongoing allure of grand historic properties.

item.title: Wilt Chamberlain’s 1971 Bel-Air estate sold for $9.7M after a 5-year overhaul & $19M listing
item.description: Basketball legend Wilt Chamberlain's Bel-Air mansion has sold for approximately $9.7 million. This sale concluded years of attempts to sell the property at a much lower price. The 9,395-square-foot home was originally commissioned by Chamberlain in 1971. After extensive renovations, the property was relisted multiple times with significant price cuts. The final sale price was nearly half of its highest asking price.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Memorial Stadium rubble built Maryland living shoreline, restoring 400ft of coast & 2 acres of wetlands
item.description: In an innovative project, crushed concrete sourced from Baltimore's Memorial Stadium has been repurposed to establish coastal foundations. This sustainable initiative has not only fostered wetland creation but has also restored over 400 linear feet of shoreline. Engineers effectively utilized the rubble to construct breakwaters and low barriers, mitigating wave erosion while simultaneously functioning as artificial reefs that bolster oyster and fish populations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UN report finds widespread sexual violence in Ukraine war, 89% of cases linked to Russia
item.description: A UN report documented widespread sexual violence by Russian forces in Ukraine. These violations included gang rape and genital mutilation against civilians and prisoners. Ukrainian authorities were responsible for a smaller number of similar human rights abuses. Most victims of sexual violence in detention were men, according to the UN findings. The report highlights the ongoing nature of these abhorrent acts amid the conflict.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: From Macaca to MAGA: How one needling remark can become a political thorn for Trump
item.description: A 2006 incident involving Senator George Allen and a racial slur highlights how small remarks can alter election outcomes. Recent social media posts by Republican Bo French have also drawn significant criticism and condemnation. These events suggest a growing unease among some Republicans regarding Trump's influence. Moderate Republicans and even prominent figures are distancing themselves from controversial rhetoric. Such shifts could impact the upcoming midterm elections and future political landscapes.

item.title: Pennsylvania teacher preserved his white pumpkin for nearly 40 years; gardeners now grow it too
item.description: Wayne Fortna, a Pennsylvania teacher, preserved a unique cream-colored pumpkin variety for decades. He found solace in gardening after serving as a tank commander during World War II. His daughter helped save the heirloom seeds through a local museum after his passing. The Landis Valley Village and Farm Museum maintained the precious seeds for future generations. Seed Savers Exchange now shares these special pumpkin seeds with gardeners worldwide.
